page: UpCloud STARTER-4xCPU-16GB is a general-purpose virtual server built on the KVM hypervisor. It features 4 vCPUs mapped to 4 physical cores of an AMD EPYC 9575F processor running at 2.0 GHz on the x86_64 architecture. The CPU allocation is shared, meaning compute resources are multiplexed. The system is equipped with 16.0 GB of system memory, providing 4.0 GB of RAM per core. Local storage consists of a bundled 50 GB SSD, and the instance includes one complimentary public IPv4 address.

In benchmark testing, the server exhibits strong single-core performance alongside moderate multi-core capabilities. The stress-ng single-core CPU test and single-threaded compression tasks (gzip and bzip3) rank in the top tier (top 10%). However, multi-core performance metrics, such as the stress-ng multi-core test and PassMark CPU score, fall into the average tier. Memory performance is a notable bottleneck, with the PassMark memory score registering in the weak tier (bottom 25%), although large-block memory read and write bandwidths maintain average-tier throughput.

Because this server utilizes a shared CPU allocation, it offers a cost-effective entry point for resource-dense workloads that do not require continuous, dedicated CPU performance. The combination of top-tier single-threaded execution and average multi-core throughput makes it suitable for lightweight web serving, Redis caching, and basic database operations. It is less suited for memory-intensive applications or larger LLM inference tasks, where its performance drops to the bottom 25%.
